title: Ramsey arrowing
description: Colour the edges of the complete graph on n nodes red and blue without a red copy of one pattern graph and without a blue copy of another; with the graphs as input, deciding whether every colouring contains a copy is Pi-2-complete (Schaefer). The check embeds a pattern into the edges of its colour, and the refinement says that one of the edges used changes colour. With n = 7 the run proves that there is no solution: the Ramsey number of a triangle and a 4-cycle is 7.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The host graph and the two pattern graphs. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
% Two pattern graphs, one per colour. pedge(Colour,P,Q): the pattern has the edge P-Q.
colour(red;blue).
pedge(red,1,2).  pedge(red,2,3).  pedge(red,1,3).                    % a red triangle
pedge(blue,1,2). pedge(blue,2,3). pedge(blue,3,4). pedge(blue,1,4).  % a blue 4-cycle
pnode(C,P) :- pedge(C,P,_).
pnode(C,P) :- pedge(C,_,P).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): colourings of the edges with two colours.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: every edge of the host graph is red or blue.
{ red(U,V) } :- edge(U,V).
#show red/2.
#show blue(U,V) : edge(U,V), not red(U,V).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: which edges are red.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a copy of a pattern in its colour (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: choose a colour and map the nodes of its pattern to different
% nodes of the host graph ...
1 { mono(C) : colour(C) } 1.
1 { map(P,V) : node(V) } 1 :- mono(C), pnode(C,P).
:- map(P,V), map(Q,V), P < Q.
% ... so that every edge of the pattern lands on an edge of that colour.
used(U,V) :- mono(C), pedge(C,P,Q), map(P,U), map(Q,V), U < V.
used(U,V) :- mono(C), pedge(C,P,Q), map(P,V), map(Q,U), U < V.
:- used(U,V), not edge(U,V).
:- used(U,V), mono(red), not red(U,V).
:- used(U,V), mono(blue), red(U,V).
#show mono/1.
#show used/2.

% The copy stays as long as the edges it uses keep their colour.
relevant(red(U,V)) :- used(U,V).

fragments.name: view
fragments.text:
% K_n; red edges red, blue edges blue; the pattern of a counterexample thick.
#program scene.
draw(layout(circle)).
draw(node(V)) :- node(V).
draw(edge(U,V)) :- edge(U,V).

#program frame.
draw(attr(edge(U,V), stroke, red)) :- cand(red(U,V)).
draw(attr(edge(U,V), stroke, blue)) :- edge(U,V), not cand(red(U,V)), kind(_).
draw(attr(edge(U,V), weight, 12)) :- cex(used(U,V)).
draw(note("A one-coloured copy of a pattern (thick): one of its edges must change colour.")) :- kind(reject).
#show draw/1.
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% The host graph: the complete graph on n nodes.
node(1..n).
edge(U,V) :- node(U), node(V), U < V.

generators.name: gnp
generators.description: A connected random graph G(n,p): each edge with probability p/1000; a disconnected draw is redrawn.
generators.text:
% gnp: a connected random graph with n nodes; each edge is present with probability p/1000
node(1..n).
edge(X,Y) :- node(X), node(Y), X < Y, @flip(p, X, Y) = 1.

reach(1).
reach(Y) :- reach(X), edge(X,Y).
reach(X) :- reach(Y), edge(X,Y).
:- node(X), not reach(X).            % a disconnected draw is rejected and redrawn

#show node/1.  #show edge/2.

generators.name: gnm
generators.description: A random graph G(n,m): exactly m of the n(n-1)/2 possible edges, chosen uniformly.
generators.text:
% gnm: m edges chosen uniformly among the pairs of n nodes (pair I is the I-th pair X < Y)
node(1..n).
pair(X,Y,(X-1)*n - (X-1)*X/2 + Y - X) :- node(X), node(Y), X < Y.
edge(X,Y) :- pair(X,Y,I), @subset(m, n*(n-1)/2, I, edges) = 1.

#show node/1.  #show edge/2.
